paras: The Sedalia police shooting of 1882 was an incident in Sedalia, Missouri, probably on the afternoon of 4 December 1882, in which Officer Wentzelman clubbed an unnamed Black man he had arrested and then fired three pistol shots at him as he fled. None of the shots hit him, and the man escaped. The only known account is a short local item in the Sedalia Weekly Bazoo, told from the officer's side.

According to the Bazoo, the man worked "out in the country" and had come into the city, where he got drunk and made himself "quite obnoxious" on West Main street. Officer Wentzelman was called to arrest him, and did so.

In front of D. H. Smith's store, the paper said, the prisoner caught hold of an iron railing, swore he would go no further and gave the officer "a tremendous shove." When Wentzelman went for him, the man, whom the paper called "a powerful fellow," struck at the officer, who dodged the blow and began using his club. After two blows to the head, the man ran up the street to Washington avenue and then north, with Wentzelman in pursuit.
In the Black neighborhood the paper called "Darkeytown," the officer drew his pistol and fired three times at the fleeing man, missing each time, and the man got away.
The coverage does not show whether the man was later caught, how badly he was hurt, or whether the officer's use of his pistol was questioned.

The Sedalia Weekly Bazoo ran the story on 5 December 1882 under the headline "He Broke Away," framing it as a prisoner's escape rather than a shooting. The item gave the officer's version as fact, did not name the man, and referred to him as "Cuffy" and to the neighborhood where he was shot at as "Darkeytown." No other paper's report of the incident has been found, and the Black press of the period is not available for comparison.
